intro: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is a volcanic island and a chain of small islands, homeland of the Garífuna people.

chapters.title: The Garífuna
text: Kalinago people and Africans who escaped shipwrecks or slavery mixed to form the Garinagu (Garífuna), who fought to keep their land.

chapters.title: British rule and exile
text: After the Carib Wars, led by Chief Joseph Chatoyer, Britain deported about 5,000 Garífuna in 1797 to Roatán, off Honduras. Their descendants now live along Central America's coast.

highlight.title: Chatoyer
highlight.text: Chief Joseph Chatoyer is the national hero.

chapters.title: Independence
text: The country became independent in 1979. La Soufrière volcano erupted in 1979 and again in 2021, forcing evacuations. Hurricane Beryl hit the Grenadines hard in 2024.
